next_mission_recommendation.mission_title: Dashboard Tab Consolidation: Merge Analytics + Lessons Learned into a unified Insights tab
next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: Now that the Semantic tab has been removed and the dashboard has been trimmed to 6 tabs, consider whether further consolidation makes sense. The Analytics tab (cost, token usage, stage timing) and Lessons Learned tab (cross-mission KB learnings) are both post-mission reflection surfaces. Merging them into a single 'Insights' tab with two sub-sections would reduce cognitive overhead when reviewing completed missions. The mission should: (1) audit current usage patterns for both tabs, (2) design a unified layout with collapsible sections for Analytics and Lessons Learned, (3) implement the merge in HTML + JS, (4) update VALID_TABS accordingly, (5) rebuild the bundle, and (6) validate with Selenium that all data still populates correctly in the merged view. The backend APIs for both tabs should remain unchanged.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: Removing the Semantic tab established a precedent for pruning unused UI surface area. The natural next step is to evaluate remaining tabs for consolidation opportunities. Analytics and Lessons Learned are both low-traffic, post-mission review tabs that would benefit from being co-located. This reduces the nav bar from 6 to 5 tabs and creates a cleaner separation between active-mission views (AtlasForge, Investigations, GlassBox) and retrospective views (Insights, Mission Logs).

final_report.summary: Successfully removed the 'Semantic' tab from the AtlasForge dashboard UI while preserving all backend functionality. The tab nav button, tab content panel, and Semantic Health mini widget were all eliminated from the rendered dashboard. A critical issue was discovered and resolved during testing: the compiled bundle.min.js was stale (pre-dating the source edits), which would have caused old browser sessions to still render the Semantic tab. The bundle was rebuilt, and a fresh Selenium session confirmed the tab is fully gone. All 7 functional tests passed. The backend API (/api/semantic/status) remains intact and operational.

challenges_overcome: Stale compiled bundle: BUILDING stage modified source files but did not rebuild dist/bundle.min.js. Browser sessions were loading the old bundle which still contained the Semantic tab. Caught during adversarial TESTING phase and resolved by running npm run build. This is a common pitfall when editing JS source files that feed into a build pipeline.

Identifying all touch points: The Semantic tab had three distinct UI components (nav button, content panel, mini widget) spread across the HTML template, plus JS-side VALID_TABS and import references that all needed coordinated removal.
lessons_learned: Always rebuild compiled assets (bundle.min.js, CSS bundles) immediately after modifying source files — do not defer to TESTING stage
When removing a UI tab, audit all three surfaces: nav entry, content panel, and any dashboard widget/shortcut references
VALID_TABS guards are the right abstraction for tab existence — removing from that list makes the fallback behavior safe automatically
Selenium fresh-session DOM inspection is the gold standard for UI removal verification — avoids false confidence from cached browser state
Backend preservation is straightforward: do not touch the blueprint registration or the Python module; only remove the frontend render paths
